documentcloud_title: 2026-07 - A-2024-01935 - Employment and Social Development Canada
documentcloud_description:
The total budget that has been allocated for ESDC’s Benefits Delivery Modernization program since January 2023 to October 2024, and an inventory of publicly visible releases since that time.   
A yearly total amount is one for "Total budget". (eg, 2022-2023: 301.4 million, etc.) A release could mean a new product or service, a new feature in an existing product or service, a significant improvement to an existing feature (eg, waiting time for X reduced by 90%), or public information about new services.   
An announcement of a future program/service/feature would not qualify as a release by this definition. Information on a release would likely be included in include any final reports and documents that accompany public deliverables (service improvements) from January 1st, 2023, to October 2024. 
In terms of the release (public service improvements) side of things, any new products/features/launches from the BDM program transmittal slips or status updates on the BDM program that include summaries of new services being launched or improvements to existing systems, that might of been captured in briefing notes to senior leaders that accompany SA&As or status updates created by BDM staff for presentations to senior leadership and BDM/TBS governance committees. The minister's LinkedIn announcement on "service delivery initiatives and improvements" which mentions "transforming benefits delivery technology" but does not specify exactly what has been released in this regard.

documentcloud_description: I am writing to request clarification regarding the eligibility criteria under the Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP) for candidates currently residing and working inside Canada. Specifically, I would like to understand how the following scenarios are assessed for eligibility and CRS (Comprehensive Ranking System) points under Express Entry: A candidate is currently working full-time in Canada for a Canadian employer on a valid work permit. The same candidate is also working full-time remotely for a foreign company (outside Canada), in a capacity that aligns with a skilled occupation under the NOC system. I seek clarification on: Whether the work experience gained with the foreign employer while physically present in Canada can be considered valid foreign work experience under FSWP. Whether the Canadian work experience gained simultaneously is counted as eligible Canadian work experience under CEC or FSWP. If both experiences (Canadian and foreign) are recognized concurrently and how they impact the CRS calculation and eligibility under Express Entry. I respectfully request access to any internal documents, policy interpretation notes, or officer guidelines that address the evaluation of such scenarios for Express Entry eligibility and CRS scoring. Only provide the final copy or the latest draft of a document. Only provide the final email in a chain of emails. (From 2020-01-01 to 2025-04-01).

April 12, 2021 - Natalie Abraham presentation “Thrombosis and Thrombocytopenia after Covid-19 vaccination in Canada” – get this presentation and presentation notes.April 15, 2021 - CAEFISS Analysis – PHAC will send VVWG an email with a breakdown of the top 3 serious AEFI rates by lot number – Karin Johnson. Get presentation from ACCA provided to VVWG. April 29, 2021 - Amanda Shaw presentation on myocarditis following Pfizer vaccine. NACI update on AstraZeneca recommendations.  Kelsey Young presentation on NACI: Update of Benefit-risk assessment for recommendation on the use of AstraZeneca Covid-19 Vaccine. May 6, 2021 - Background Rates Update – Sarah Spruin. Group question – Yukon questioned Inflammatory flare-up of autoimmune disease, when not pre-existing in young people.
